title: SLO priority deconflict and capacity runway initiative
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a pragmatic 60->120 day cross-functional plan to: (1) establish a lightweight SLO priority deconflict process, (2) create a capacity runway model tied to SLO tiers, and (3) land a small set of automation + rituals that reduce firefighting and make tradeoffs explicit across product, infra, and platform teams.

Why now:
- Growing surface area of model-serving endpoints (hosted + dedicated) means competing latency/cost demands.
- Recent incidents surfaced that teams were implicitly racing for capacity and dialing batch/quantization without product alignment.
- We need a repeatable way to 1) decide what to protect, 2) size runway, and 3) automate fallback/route policies for graceful degradation.

Success metrics (what success looks like):
- A documented, adopted SLO priority rubric used by 8 pilot services within 60 days.
- Capacity runway model prototype that maps committed reserve GPUs to error-budget burn rates and burst probability (first-pass Monte Carlo).
- Two automations: prefix-based KV cache hit metric alert + automated model-variant fallback policy implemented for 1 mission-critical route.
- Fewer priority escalations: target 40% reduction in cross-team capacity disputes in quarter after rollout (measured by severity-2 ops tickets tagged "capacity-deconflict").

Scope and out-of-scope:
In scope:
- SLO tiering rubric, priority deconflict flow, and decision board (simple RACI + triage steps).
- Capacity runway model (spreadsheet prototype -> small Python sim) and visualization widget for Console dashboard.
- Small automation tasks tied to reducing last-mile manual fallbacks (two runbooks + one policy automation).
- Cross-team on-call and escalation handshake for canary rollouts tied to SLO gates.
Out of scope:
- Full re-architecture of serving runtime.
- Enterprise SLA contract/legal renegotiation (we will surface gaps).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Eng SRE (lead): Anika Patel (owner) — coordinate model, run experiments, own runway sim and metrics.
- Serving Runtime: Ravi Desai — validate model assumptions about batching, KV cache behavior; implement sampling hooks.
- Product: Leah Morgan — prioritize feature routes, translate product cost/latency tradeoffs into SLO impact statements.
- Platform/Capacity: Jordan Kim — map GPU pool commitments and bursting policies; provide cost inputs.
- Observability: Carlos Rivera — add dashboards/alerts, ensure traceability to token-level latency/cost.
- Solutions & CS (pilot customers): TBD (engage 2 existing customers for pilot feedback).

High-level timeline (60 -> 120 days):
Phase 0 (this week): kickoff, align stakeholders, choose 6-8 pilot routes.
Phase 1 (weeks 1-4): lightweight rubric + decision flow; spreadsheet runway prototype.
- Deliverables: SLO-rubric doc, pilot route list, runway spreadsheet with baseline inputs.
Phase 2 (weeks 5-8): implement sampling hooks + baseline telemetry; iterate runway sim with real metrics.
- Deliverables: telemetry dashboard, Monte Carlo sim v1, runbook drafts.
Phase 3 (weeks 9-12): policy automation PoC (one route): fallback to cheaper quantized model / region-burst path; tie to SLO gates.
- Deliverables: automation PR, canary rollout plan, incident playbook.
Phase 4 (weeks 13-16): retro, sweep, handoff for broader adoption; priority board and lightweight governance.
- Deliverables: adoption checklist, comms plan, success metric report.

Detailed artifacts to create (short summary):
1) SLO Priority Rubric (doc): Inputs: user impact, revenue exposure, legal/regulatory weight, latency sensitivity, beta feature flag. Outputs: SLO tier (critical/high/medium/low), suggested runways and fallback policies.
2) Decision Board (spreadsheet / small Confluence page): current requests for capacity + active burn rate + proposed mitigations.
3) Capacity Runway Prototype (sheet + small sim): maps pool capacity -> error budget exhaustion curves for different traffic spikes.
4) Telemetry additions: sample traces for model variants, token-level latency distributions, per-route prefix cache hit rate, and kv-cache eviction counters.
5) Automation PoC: model-variant routing policy that can be toggled via Console (lab-only first).
6) Runbooks: triage checklist, rollback checklist, customer communication templates.

Decision flow (quick sketch):
- Product raises request (Jira) or SRE detects high burn.
- Decision board triage (weekly): product + platform + SRE review, assign tier using rubric.
- If tier critical -> immediate allocation or mandatory canary with SLO gates.
- If tier high -> recommend reserved capacity + 72h runway; if not available, require explicit product trade-off sign-off.
- Medium/low -> queue for next capacity planning cycle or suggest throttling/caching.

Rituals and cadence:
- Weekly SLO triage (30m): quick list of active escalations, burn trends, and decisions. Mandatory: product owner and platform lead.
- Biweekly runway review (60m): deeper dive into capacity forecast, simulated exhaustion scenarios.
- Ad-hoc on-call handshake during canary (15m pre-launch + 60m watch).
- Monthly report to Eng Leadership: top 5 SLO burns, root causes, capacity actions taken.

Measurement and telemetry plan:
- Core signals: per-route error budget burn rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency, KV cache hit rate per prefix, model-variant selection counts, burst queue length.
- Alerts: error budget burn > x% in y minutes triggers triage; runway depletion projection < 72h triggers capacity request.
- Dashboards: visible in Console with one-click drilldowns into traces and cost estimates.

Experiment matrix (small):
- A/B fallback to quantized variant (measure latency, quality regression delta, cost delta).
- Prefix caching tuned by TTL vs. request distribution.
- Autoscale policy variations (conservative vs aggressive) and effect on SLOs and cost.
- Each experiment: hypothesis, metric, duration (2 weeks), owner.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quality gating for model-variant fallback: what automatic checks do we need to avoid user-impacting regressions? (Leah + Applied ML to define).
- Which pilot customers are ok with being in a canary that may see degraded quality temporarily? (CS to confirm).
- Where do cost approvals live if platform needs to spin up temporary reserved capacity? (Finance signoff loop).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: False confidence from spreadsheet sim. Mitigation: feed real telemetry quickly and run stochastic sims; mark sim outputs as "experimental".
- Risk: Product pushback when fallback affects UX. Mitigation: require product sign-off, instrument quality comparison and rollback hooks.
- Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: Carlos to prioritize adding minimal traces and counters in first sprint.

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Kickoff sync: 30m (Anika, Ravi, Leah, Jordan, Carlos) — schedule by EOD Mon.
- Identify 6 pilot routes and capture current SLOs + telemetry (owners assign by Wed).
- Spin up runway spreadsheet with baseline capacity numbers and rough burn rates (Anika + Jordan).
- Create the JIRA epic and link to this doc: JIRA-REL-342 (owner: Anika).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Keep the rubric intentionally simple — two pages max. We can iterate after pilots.
- Try to map runway not only to GPUs but to other bottlenecks (redis cache size, KV eviction rate).
- Consider a simple "grace credits" concept: short-term borrowed capacity that triggers automatic billing alert and requires postmortem.

Appendix: quick SLO tier draft (example)
- Critical: user-facing payment flows, admin controls, regulatory data access. SLO: 99.95% availability p99 latency target. Runway: 168h (7d) recommended.
- High: core product search/chat features. SLO: 99.9% p95 latency. Runway: 72h.
- Medium: background enrichment, non-urgent analytics. SLO: 99% p95 latency. Runway: 24-48h.
- Low: developer tooling / internal experiments. SLO: best-effort. Runway: none / queue.

Contact and ownership:
- Doc owner: Anika Patel (eng-sre).
- Primary reviewer: Ravi Desai (serving-runtime).
- Observability contact: Carlos Rivera.

If you have edits, drop them inline or add comments — this is intentionally a working doc.
